ShortDescription.Value: One bar showing the state of your city, where every reading opens what it is about.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Seety
Maybe the real city was the stats we saw along the way.
## Setup
1. Enable the mod. 2. In the options, on Seety's **Readings** tab, tick the readings you want. 3. To move the bar, untick **Lock the bar in place** on the **Bar** tab, drag it, and tick it again.
The bar can also run vertically, from the same tab.
## The bar
**Twenty-six readings**, each on or off as you like. Click one and it takes you to what it is about: most open the matching info view, the rest open a window of their own - draggable, closeable.
- **Active problems** - every notification by type, worst first; click a type to fly to each one in turn. Can hide the icons over the city. - **Happiness and demographics** - average happiness, and who lives here by age and education. - **Average health** - with hospital coverage beside it. - **Unemployment** and **homelessness** - the share of citizens affected. - **Workers** - your workforce against the jobs that exist, level by level: employed, idle, overqualified, commuting. - **Tourists** - how many are in town. - **Electricity**, **water** and **sewage** - how much of the demand is actually met, with batteries and trade in the window. - **Crematorium coverage** and **cemetery space** - which cemetery is about to fill, one click away. - **Four school levels** - free places, fullest schools first. - **Free parking** - room left for cars and bikes. - **Garbage processing** - with landfill space beside it. - **Safety from crime** - with free jail and prison cells beside it. - **Fire safety**, **postal service** and **land value**. - **Environment quality** - the four pollutions, each opening its own map. - **Traffic flow** - the worst jams, the transit lines standing still, or the route of whatever you have selected. - **Zone demand** - all six demands and the biggest reasons behind each, down to the resource. - **Transport passengers** - passengers and freight by mode, and the busiest stops.
Some readings also carry a chart of how they got here.
Optionally, rest the cursor on a building to see what is holding it back, and by how much.
## What it never does
Seety reads. It does not govern. Clicking a reading changes only which info view is showing and where the camera is pointing.
Two options draw outside Seety's own bar, both off unless you turn them on: one prints the change beside the population and money figures on the bottom bar; the other redraws the game's blue buttons in the bottom bar's colour.
Two other exceptions, both on the options page and nowhere near the bar. One is a field to add or remove money from your treasury, City Watchdog style - off to the side, typed in on purpose. The other fades the zoning cells drawn along your roads, for anyone who finds them loud: off unless you turn it on, it changes how those cells are drawn and nothing else, and switching it back off restores exactly the colours the game shipped.
## Before you install
Available in all twelve languages supported by the game. Free and open source under the MIT licence: [source on GitHub](https://github.com/merrinaf-tech/Seety).
If it saves you a few trips through the menus, you can [buy me a coffee](https://ko-fi.com/fabiozsche). Entirely optional - the mod is the same either way.
Publish.ChangeLog: Readings are chosen in the options, on their own tab. Option for a vertical bar. The bar is locked in place; unlock it in the options to move it. The bar snaps into line with the game's buttons. Info view panels draw over the bar.
